scope: Proposition 3.1 of the manuscript “The Restricted Geometric Langlands Equivalence in Positive Characteristic” (preprints/The-Restricted-Geometric-Langlands-Equivalence-in-Positive-Characteristic-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 52c37d4f70f505c0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let k and G satisfy Hypothesis 1.1 and either Hypothesis 1.2 or Hypothe- sis 1.3, and let κ be the invariant symmetric form in those hypotheses. Suppose that a(t) ∈ g[[t]] satisfies χ(a(0)) ̸= χ(0). After a change of frame by an element of G(k[[t]]), there are a Levi subgroup M ⊂ G and a cocharacter λ : Gm → Z(M) such that a(t) ∈ m[[t]], κ(a(0), dλ) ̸= 0, ada(0) : g/m −→ g/m is invertible. (3.1) Here adx(y) = [x, y]. The subgroup M may equal G, and the invertibility assertion includes the zero vector space.
